features.name: any_sequenced_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment lay out its reasoning in an explicit ordered sequence (e.g., first... then... second...)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment itself presents its own argument as an explicit logical sequence with ordinal/sequential markers (e.g., first/firstly, then, second/secondly, third, finally, step by step) structuring its reasoning points. Markers must organize the commenter's own argument; sequences only in quoted text from others, or unrelated lists, do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, outcome reports or post-outcome updates as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies or the list is empty; null if missing/malformed. List order is not chronology.

h0: any_sequenced_counterargument has no association with delta.
h1: Rows with any_sequenced_counterargument = 1 have higher delta rates than rows with 0.
note: "More persuasive" is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). Row-level "any comment" is an assumption; the hypothesis does not specify any/share. Association only; reply timing unknown and comments lack individual outcomes, so the specific sequenced comment cannot be linked to persuasion. Comment text may contain outcome announcements; the prompt excludes them.
